matrixNote: Resources needed by use-case archetype. ● = needed for every use case of that type; ○ = needed for some. Coding is team judgement from the 90 catalogue use cases (the AI-use-policy row is governance, not a tool, and is left out).

intensity.Light: a SaaS tool or AI licence that works with little integration; low risk; mostly staff time.
intensity.Moderate: needs two-way links to core systems (PMS, POS, CRM) and clean data; subscription or usage fees; a human checks output.
intensity.Heavy: hardware or building-system investment, a group data platform, multi-system agents, or high legal risk (biometrics, recruitment, employee monitoring).

readme: For each of the 91 use cases in the Hotel AI Use-Case Catalogue (D4 artifact, 15 departments), the resources a hotel needs, split into the six D6 areas: people, skills, financial investment, technology infrastructure, data, organisation & governance.
1. Use case, AI type, hotel use level and category are copied from the catalogue as of 12 Nov 2026.

2. The six resource cells apply the D6 requirements (D6 Word report, section 3) to what each use case does: which systems it reads and writes, which data it needs, whether it buys hardware, and how risky its output is.

3. Evidence IDs point to rows in the D6 evidence pack (master v8_3) that speak to this use case or its department. "—" means no use-case-specific evidence: the row is team judgement from the catalogue description plus cross-cutting D6 requirements. Treat it as a hypothesis to test in interviews.
4. "Checklist items to check first" use the codes of the D6 readiness checklist (31 questions; gates: P1, F1, F2, T1, D5, O1).
Light: a SaaS tool or AI licence that works with little integration; low risk; mostly staff time.
Moderate: needs two-way links to core systems (PMS, POS, CRM) and clean data; subscription or usage fees; a human checks output.
Heavy: hardware or building-system investment, a group data platform, multi-system agents, or high legal risk (biometrics, recruitment, employee monitoring).
Legal points (EU AI Act Art. 50 disclosure, Art. 5 prohibitions, Annex III high-risk employment uses; GDPR Art. 9 biometrics; PCI DSS) are signposts only. Detail and confirmation belong in D7.

No source in the evidence gives costs or staffing per use case for European hotels. Intensity and resource cells are qualitative. Counts and IDs come from master v8_3 and should be refreshed from v8_4.
